core_obligations: Part (1), the induction (proof lines 12633-12660): write the hypothesis as the vanishing of H^i(K tensor^L O/I) for i > b, use the distinguished triangle K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1} -> K tensor^L O/I^{n+1} -> K tensor^L O/I^n and its rotation, and the identification K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1} = (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} I^n/I^{n+1}, to propagate the vanishing H^i(K tensor^L O/I^n) = 0 for i > b to n + 1; this gives uniform boundedness above for all n.

Part (2), reduction to O/I-modules (proof lines 12663-12676): for a sheaf F of O/I^n-modules use the finite filtration 0 subset I^{n-1}F subset ... subset IF subset F with successive quotients O/I-modules, so that tor amplitude in [a, b] of K tensor^L O/I^n follows once H^i(K tensor^L O/I^n tensor^L_{O/I^n} G) vanishes for i outside [a, b] and every O/I-module G.

Part (2), the identification of the tensor products (proof lines 12677-12686): use (K tensor^L O/I^n) tensor^L_{O/I^n} G = (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} G for every O/I-module G, so that the required vanishing is exactly the tor amplitude hypothesis and the result follows.
proof_roadmap: For (1), assume H^i(K tensor^L O/I) = 0 for i > b.
Use the distinguished triangle of K tensor^L - applied to 0 -> I^n/I^{n+1} -> O/I^{n+1} -> O/I^n -> 0, plus the base-change identification of K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1}, to induct on n.
For (2), let F be an O/I^n-module and use the finite filtration by the powers of I with O/I-module quotients.
Then it suffices to know H^i(K tensor^L O/I^n tensor^L G) = 0 outside [a, b] for O/I-modules G.
Rewrite that tensor product as (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} G and apply the hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: The lemma transfers boundedness and tor amplitude from K tensor^L O/I to K tensor^L O/I^n uniformly in n (statement lines 12614-12630). Part (1) is an induction on n using the distinguished triangles coming from 0 -> I^n/I^{n+1} -> O/I^{n+1} -> O/I^n -> 0 and the base-change identification of K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1} as (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} I^n/I^{n+1}, which is what makes the bound independent of n (proof lines 12637-12660). Part (2) needs an additional reduction, since the test modules in the definition of tor amplitude are O/I^n-modules: one uses the finite filtration of such a module by the powers of I with O/I-module quotients, then rewrites (K tensor^L O/I^n) tensor^L_{O/I^n} G as (K tensor^L O/I) tensor^L_{O/I} G (proof lines 12666-12686). The claim is H2: two explicit reductions, each short once the right triangle and the right filtration are chosen.
